text:
objective: Predictive modelling of the spatial pattern of past and future forest cover changes in India
country: India
land_use_classes: Forest; Non-Forest
baseline_years: 1930; 1975; 1995; 2005; 2013
target_future_years: 1880; 2025
scenarios: Business-as-usual (BAU)
analysis_methods: Change detection analysis; Transition potentials modelling; Multi-layer perceptron neural network; Markov-cellular automata (MCA) model; Rate of deforestation calculation
simulation_method_advantages: LCM considers driver data for change prediction, improving accuracy over methods like Markov chain which only gives temporal dynamics; CA-Markov combines temporal and spatial pattern simulation
predictors: Elevation; Slope; Distance to roads; Distance to settlements; Distance to water bodies
population_selected: Not specified
data_sources: Multi-temporal classified forest cover data from National Remote Sensing Centre (National Carbon Project); Historical archives; Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) DEM
tools_software_used: Land Change Modeler (LCM) in IDRISI Selva software
validation_performed: Yes
validation_methods: Comparison of simulated forest cover map (2013) with actual forest cover map (2013); Computation of Cohen's Kappa statistic from confusion table
validation_data_sources: Actual classified forest cover map for 2013
key_findings: Predicted forest cover in 1880 was 1,042,008 km2 (31.7% of India); About 40% of forest cover lost during 1880–2013; Six Northeastern states and Andaman & Nicobar Islands had annual gross deforestation rate >0.3 (2005-2013); Model predicted further decrease of 2305 km2 of forest in these regions by 2025; Majority of protected areas successful in protection except Manas, Sonai-Rupai, Nameri and Marat Longri; Deforestation rate higher at lower elevations; Model predicted with Kappa statistic >0.70
implications: Useful for effective resource management, biodiversity conservation, and mitigating climate change; Supports REDD+ Programme; Can aid in declaration of new protected areas and regional planning
limitations: Not specified
future_directions: Not specified
scalability: Not specified
novelty: Spatio-temporal pattern analysis of forest cover distribution and deforestation in India based on remote sensing and Artificial Neural Networks of LCM; Reconstruction of past forest cover for 1880 and prediction for 2025
